key_decisions.rationale:
Scanner.cs:162-166 flags a folder Unreadable after appending its partial listing, and Scanner.cs:182 passes `error != 0` to TopLevelTracker.FolderExited. That sets OwnUnreadable (TopLevelTracker.cs:91), which becomes TopLevelState.Unreadable (TopLevelTracker.cs:172), which TopLevelRowText.cs:29 words as '(could not be opened)'; lines 39-40 word UnreadableBelow the same way. CancelledFolderTests.cs:269-271 pins such a folder as Unreadable(995) with 1 to 1999 children kept. SL-044's review m1 fixed the wording in the tree only.
Fix: Use one wording rule for a partial listing everywhere. Give TopLevelRow a flag for 'listed partway',…

key_decisions.decision: HF-004 at src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs:47: The private field _result is assigned in ShowOutcome and cleared in StartScan, and nothing reads it. LastResult already holds the same ScanResult and is cleared on the same line. The field's only effect is a second root keeping the finished store alive, and the comment at the clear ('let the previous scan's store be collected') suggests it matters when it does not.
key_decisions.rationale:
`git grep -n -E "_result\b" -- src tests eng` returns only MainWindow.xaml.cs:47 (the declaration), :194 (`_result = null;`) and :441 (`_result = result;`). The hook reads LastResult by reflection (TreeMode.cs:506), never _result.
Fix: Delete the field and its two assignments.

ShowOutcome then calls ShowFolderTree, which sets the list's ItemsSource to null, hides the list and writes its own header. The Completed branch of the header is never what a c…
key_decisions.rationale:
MainWindow.xaml.cs:247 calls `ShowFinalTopLevel(failure is null ? result?.TopLevel : null)` for every non-failed result. Lines 319-339 do the sort, the ItemsSource bind and the header, with the Completed branch at 329-331. Lines 480-481 call ShowFolderTree on a Completed scan, and lines 378-383 null ItemsSource, collapse the list and overwrite TopLevelHeader. WindowReport.cs:67-69 and SL-044 say topLevel is absent after a completed scan 'because the list holds nothing'.
Fix: In StartScan, call ShowFinalTopLevel only when result.Status != Completed; for a completed scan, call ClearTopLevel and let ShowFolderTree fill the cell. Then remove the Completed branch from ShowTopLevel's header.

Because of that, FolderTreeRowText cannot be compiled into Core.Tests by link the way StoppingWait is, and its midpoint rounding and 1-pixel bar floor…
key_decisions.rationale:
FolderTreeRowText.cs:14 is `internal static string Size(long bytes) => MainWindow.FormatSize(bytes);`. TopLevelRowText.cs:36 and 40 call MainWindow.FormatSize and MainWindow.Count directly. FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj:27-31 links StoppingWait.cs, a pure App helper, into Core.Tests. FolderTreeRowText.cs:22-30 holds the Share and BarWidth logic.
Fix: Move FormatSize (and Count) out of MainWindow into a small pure text class, for example SizeText.cs. Let FolderTreeNode and TopLevelRowText call it directly and delete the forwarder. Link that class and FolderTreeRowText into Core.Tests as StoppingWait is, so Share and BarWidth get unit tests.

key_decisions.decision: HF-019 at src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs:107: The window's size and position assume it opens on the primary monitor. SystemParameters.WorkArea is the primary display's work area. When Windows places the window on a monitor arranged below the primary (Top >= the primary's Bottom), `Top + Height > area.Bottom` is always true. Top is then set to area.Bottom - Height, which moves the window onto the primary monitor's rows. On a secondary monitor…
key_decisions.rationale:
Lines 62 (`Height = Math.Min(Height, SystemParameters.WorkArea.Height)`) and 110-112 compare only against SystemParameters.WorkArea. A scratch run (.health-scratch/wpfprobe2) showed Top is set by OnSourceInitialized (Top=26, WorkArea=0,0,1920,1032), so the move runs on every launch. Only one monitor was available here, so the multi-monitor case was not run.
Fix: Use the work area of the monitor the window is on: MonitorFromWindow plus GetMonitorInfo on the HWND in OnSourceInitialized, or the Screen API. Clamp and move against that monitor's rcWork, converted to DIPs.

That copies and sorts the whole final snapshot on the UI thread (up to 100,000 rows) and binds it to TopLevelList. ShowOutcome then calls ShowFolderTree, which sets TopLevelList.ItemsSource = null and collapses the list right away. The sort and bind are wasted UI-thread work during the…
key_decisions.rationale:
MainWindow.xaml.cs:247 `ShowFinalTopLevel(failure is null ? result?.TopLevel : null)`. Then 319-339 (ShowTopLevel: `[.. snapshot.Rows]`, Array.Sort, ItemsSource = rows, BeginInvoke(Loaded, ...)). Then 480-481 `if (finished) ShowFolderTree(result)` -> 378-380 `TopLevelList.ItemsSource = null; TopLevelList.Visibility = Collapsed; _shownTopLevel = null`. SL-039 measured one such refresh at 25-46 ms p95 for 100k rows.
Fix: Skip the final list refresh when the scan completed: `ShowFinalTopLevel(failure is null && result?.Status != ScanStatus.Completed ? result?.TopLevel : null)`. Only when it completed, clear the list with ClearTopLevel instead.

health_findings.claim: A folder whose listing failed partway keeps the entries it listed, and they are counted. The results list, shown during a scan and after a stop, calls that folder 'could not be opened', and its 'N folders inside could not be opened' count includes such folders. The folder tree calls the same state 'could not be read in full'. The largest-files caption says 'Files in N unreadable folders are not included', but the files listed before the error are included. The same state reads differently on different screens, and two of the texts are false.
health_findings.evidence:
Scanner.cs:162-166 flags a folder Unreadable after appending its partial listing, and Scanner.cs:182 passes `error != 0` to TopLevelTracker.FolderExited. That sets OwnUnreadable (TopLevelTracker.cs:91), which becomes TopLevelState.Unreadable (TopLevelTracker.cs:172), which TopLevelRowText.cs:29 words as '(could not be opened)'; lines 39-40 word UnreadableBelow the same way. FolderTreeNode.cs:66-70 splits the state into 'could not be read in full' (ChildCount > 0) and 'could not be opened'. MainWindow.xaml.cs:521-522 has the caption. CancelledFolderTests.cs:269-271 pins such a folder as Unreadable(995) with 1 to 1999 children kept. SL-044's review m1 fixed the wording in the tree only.
Fix: Use one wording rule for a partial listing everywhere. Give TopLevelRow a flag for 'listed partway', or use a separate TopLevelState, so TopLevelRowText can say 'could not be read in full' as FolderTreeNode.Note does. Word the largest-files caption as 'folders that could not be read (in full)'.
(seen by structure)

health_findings.claim: Since SL-044, a Completed ending still goes through ShowFinalTopLevel, which copies and sorts every top-level row, binds them to the list and writes the SL-039 Completed header ('Largest at the top of X' or 'X is empty.'). ShowOutcome then calls ShowFolderTree, which sets the list's ItemsSource to null, hides the list and writes its own header. The Completed branch of the header is never what a completed ending leaves on screen. The sort and reset are work thrown away during the hand-off: at M-001's 100,000 top-level folders, that is 100,000 rows sorted before the tree sorts the same children again.
health_findings.evidence:
MainWindow.xaml.cs:247 calls `ShowFinalTopLevel(failure is null ? result?.TopLevel : null)` for every non-failed result. Lines 319-339 do the sort, the ItemsSource bind and the header, with the Completed branch at 329-331. Lines 480-481 call ShowFolderTree on a Completed scan, and lines 378-383 null ItemsSource, collapse the list and overwrite TopLevelHeader. WindowReport.cs:67-69 and SL-044 say topLevel is absent after a completed scan 'because the list holds nothing'.
Fix: In StartScan, call ShowFinalTopLevel only when result.Status != Completed; for a completed scan, call ClearTopLevel and let ShowFolderTree fill the cell. Then remove the Completed branch from ShowTopLevel's header.

health_findings.claim: The delete-first step deletes an existing report at <file> before the run. If that file is read-only, or open without share-delete, File.Delete throws. The catch at line 69 exits 3 (CannotWriteReport) and leaves the old report where it was. WindowReport.cs:26 promises 'Every non-zero exit leaves no file at <file>', so after this exit 3, a stale report from an earlier run sits at the path a caller will read.
health_findings.evidence:
Checked the mechanism with .NET: [System.IO.File]::Delete on a read-only file under .health-scratch threw 'UnauthorizedAccessException: Access to the path ... is denied.', and 'still there: True'. App.xaml.cs:62-73 catches IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException and calls Shutdown(CannotWriteReport) without further cleanup.

App.xaml.cs:51-73: GetFullPath, a check that the folder exists, then `File.Delete(report); File.Delete(report + ".tmp");`. The argument checks follow at lines 77-81. WindowReport.cs:25-27 makes 'Every non-zero exit leaves no file at <file>' the reason for deleting first, but nothing limits the delete to a report file.
Fix: Clear the read-only attribute before deleting (File.SetAttributes(report, FileAttributes.Normal) when the file exists). Or narrow the contract in WindowReport.cs so it promises only that no exit writes a report of its own, not that the path is empty.
(seen by find:1:1, find:1:2)

health_findings.claim: The window's size and position assume it opens on the primary monitor. SystemParameters.WorkArea is the primary display's work area. When Windows places the window on a monitor arranged below the primary (Top >= the primary's Bottom), `Top + Height > area.Bottom` is always true. Top is then set to area.Bottom - Height, which moves the window onto the primary monitor's rows. On a secondary monitor taller than the primary, line 62 also clamps Height to the primary's work-area height.
health_findings.evidence:
Lines 62 (`Height = Math.Min(Height, SystemParameters.WorkArea.Height)`) and 110-112 compare only against SystemParameters.WorkArea. A scratch run (.health-scratch/wpfprobe2) showed Top is set by OnSourceInitialized (Top=26, WorkArea=0,0,1920,1032), so the move runs on every launch. Only one monitor was available here, so the multi-monitor case was not run.
Fix: Use the work area of the monitor the window is on: MonitorFromWindow plus GetMonitorInfo on the HWND in OnSourceInitialized, or the Screen API. Clamp and move against that monitor's rcWork, converted to DIPs.
(seen by find:1:1)

health_findings.claim: At a Completed ending, StartScan calls ShowFinalTopLevel(result.TopLevel) before the ending's status is checked. That copies and sorts the whole final snapshot on the UI thread (up to 100,000 rows) and binds it to TopLevelList. ShowOutcome then calls ShowFolderTree, which sets TopLevelList.ItemsSource = null and collapses the list right away. The sort and bind are wasted UI-thread work during the hand-off that SL-044 measured at 105-136 ms. The ShowTopLevel callback posted at Loaded priority then records LastRefresh and arms _skipNextRefresh for a list that is no longer shown.
health_findings.evidence:
MainWindow.xaml.cs:247 `ShowFinalTopLevel(failure is null ? result?.TopLevel : null)`. Then 319-339 (ShowTopLevel: `[.. snapshot.Rows]`, Array.Sort, ItemsSource = rows, BeginInvoke(Loaded, ...)). Then 480-481 `if (finished) ShowFolderTree(result)` -> 378-380 `TopLevelList.ItemsSource = null; TopLevelList.Visibility = Collapsed; _shownTopLevel = null`. SL-039 measured one such refresh at 25-46 ms p95 for 100k rows.
Fix: Skip the final list refresh when the scan completed: `ShowFinalTopLevel(failure is null && result?.Status != ScanStatus.Completed ? result?.TopLevel : null)`. Only when it completed, clear the list with ClearTopLevel instead.
